tagline: Down at area. Champion at state.
headline: Texas Track & Field · 800m & Cross Country

school.name: The University of Texas at Austin

bio.short: McKale Lee is a freshman middle-distance runner for Texas and the 2026 UIL 6A state champion in the 800m. A year after falling at the area meet, she won state in 2:08.69. She studies Exercise Science and was a 2026 Project Manager Intern at Feniex Industries.
long: McKale Lee runs the 800m and cross country for the University of Texas. In May 2026 she won the UIL Class 6A state title in the 800m at Mike A. Myers Stadium in Austin, clocking 2:08.69 to finish more than two seconds clear of the field. That spring she also won the Region III 800m, took second in the regional 1600m and swept the 800m and 1600m at the area meet, where her 2:08.50 was the fastest girls' 800m run in Texas all year. As a Longhorn freshman she set personal bests at 6K and 5K in her first college cross country season.

She grew up in Houston and ran for Alief Taylor High School, where a fall on the back straight at the 2025 area meet ended her junior season short of state. Her answer became her motto: "If you fall seven times, get back up eight times." Twelve months later she was a state champion, and she dedicated the title to her community in Southwest Alief. She now studies Exercise Science at Texas.

In 2026 she joined Feniex Industries, the Austin maker of emergency-vehicle lighting, sirens and controllers, as a Project Manager Intern. The habits that carried her back from that fall fit the job: she works to a plan, measures progress honestly and stays steady when the schedule tightens. Middle-distance racing is a constant series of pacing and timing decisions made under pressure, the same judgment a project manager uses to keep work moving between engineering, production and sales.
